title: CST Studio MCP
headline: From a tool call to a trustworthy operation.
intro: A reliability-focused bridge between CST Studio Suite and MCP clients, covering connection timing, error propagation, and the simulation lifecycle.
diagram_alt: Three layers connecting an MCP client, the server, and CST
diagram_caption: Architecture flow. A successful tool call is not the same as a completed and validated simulation.
status: Reliability fixes merged; 56 tests passed on each of two MCP SDK versions.
finding_title: A server that reports operation state accurately.
finding: The review found CST connections occurring before the client handshake, some failures being returned as successful calls, and inconsistent solver lifecycle behavior.

work.title: Client connection
work.body: Standard MCP handshake, tool discovery, and calls, with the stdio protocol channel kept separate from logs.

work.title: CST lifecycle
work.body: Blocking and asynchronous solver calls are distinguished, while status queries remain read-only.

work.title: Actionable errors
work.body: Failures reach the client as failures, and an ambiguous operation state is preserved when a timeout occurs.

verified: 56 tests passed with MCP SDK 1.29.0 and 56 with 2.2.0; 180 tool schemas were validated.
Handshake, tool discovery, calls, and separation of Python/native logs were tested through a real stdio subprocess.
A fake CST backend verified busy, timeout, unknown solver state, safe disconnect, and result-error propagation.
limits: All 180 tools have not been executed against a real CST installation, and correctness is not claimed for every client or CST release.
The running research experiment was preserved; this work did not run a new end-to-end solve in real CST.
next: For a new setup, add the MCP server first and then connect explicitly with cst_connect. A real-CST check should later use an empty session and a temporary project. The verified scope is recorded in docs/RELIABILITY_REVIEW.md in the repository.
